eva: Quick flag 10:35 UTC: console p95 for /v1/generate shot from ~160ms -> 510ms for a 5m window. Sample count steady. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/def456 :eyes:

miguel: any routing changes around then?

ops-bot: routing-policy-service promoted rollout v5 -> v6 at 2024-10-05T10:33:12Z by @deploy-bot :rocket:

eva: rollout increased fallback route weight from 5% -> 30% at that time.

sara: if fallback is slower but small volume it can skew p95 once it crosses the tail. Do we split percentiles by sample provenance anywhere?

hana: not really. Our backend compacts tdigest rollups and we currently collapse route dimension for storage efficiency. That means frontend percentiles are across merged samples.

james: two quick product ideas: 1) overlay a thin "provenance ribbon" under percentile lines showing route mix (stacked colors = primary/fallback/retries). 2) add an "SLO mode" toggle that excludes retries from percentile calc.

eva: good. I ran metrics API queries manually: ```GET /metrics?endpoint=/v1/generate&window=5m&include_retries=true``` p95=510ms; ```...&include_retries=false``` p95=170ms. So retries are the big delta here.

miguel: where are retries attributed? gateway or runtime? if gateway retries are double-counted, that matters.

hana: retries are initiated by gateway on upstream_timeout and get a header X-Retry-Reason=upstream_timeout. We tag the metric with retry=true and set route=fallback when it goes to fallback.

sara: short-term: can the console render an event marker for routing weight changes? Even without per-route percentiles, an annotation helps root cause.

miguel: backend change to emit routing events to the metrics events stream is trivial. The harder part is preserving a small route id in rollups to allow split percentiles later. I can prototype adding a one-byte route_id to tdigest bucket index. Need to run storage delta.

james: UX: label the toggle clearly: "Exclude gateway retries (recommended for SLO-aligned percentiles)". Also add a tooltip explaining that routing changes can temporarily spike tail percentiles.

eva: i'll add a 3-step triage snippet to internal runbook: 1) check recent routing events; 2) toggle exclude_retries; 3) inspect per-route sample counts in raw logs.

sara: i'll pick up the frontend annotation + toggle PR. I'll stub the api param and default to current behavior.

miguel: i'll run the storage impact calc and post numbers here. If route_id costs <10% storage we can do it in the next ingest rollout.

hana: implementation note: merging route dim earlier was to avoid cardinality blowup. route_id approach keeps cardinality bounded since ids map to known routes. We'll also need a migration plan for historical rollups.

eva: ha, ignore the typo. tagging @sara @miguel @james for follow-ups. I'll leave this thread open for PR links and the storage calc. :thumbsup:
